rounds.text: Aarnav Fashions Ltd trades at a compelling discount, with a price-to-book ratio of 0.68x against a book value of ₹ 47.3 [E2], and a P/B ratio below the sector benchmark of 1.21x [E7]. A discounted cash flow model puts intrinsic value at ₹ 59 per share compared to the market price of ₹ 32, offering a substantial margin of safety of 45.9% [E42, E43]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that today's price implies only 5.5% earnings growth, well below the 14.0% base-case assumption [E44]. Operational generation is remarkably robust, highlighted by a cash conversion ratio of 2.33x for March 2026 where operating cash flow reached ₹ 21 Cr, fully backing reported profits [E33, E34]. Historical execution is also evident in a 10-year compounded sales growth of 96% and a 10-year compounded profit growth of 77% [E14, E18]. Conceded: Promoter holding has decreased by 5.91 percentage points since December 2023, and TTD compounded profit growth sits at -12% [E21, E39].

Aarnav Fashions Ltd carries significant structural and operational weaknesses that undermine its surface-level low valuation multiples. Profitability is persistently anaemic, highlighted by a median return on equity of just 4% over 10, 5, and 3-year periods [E25, E26, E27], and a recent ROE of 4.21% that trails the sector benchmark of 6.77% [E9]. Furthermore, top-line and bottom-line growth show severe recent deterioration, marked by a -12% contraction in compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E21] alongside quarterly screen metrics indicating a net profit drop of -30% YoY and sales down -4% YoY [E65, E66]. Leverage is rising as borrowings increased to Rs 124 Cr in Sep 2026 from Rs 109 Cr a year earlier [E37], while insider confidence is ebbing given that promoter holdings have declined by 5.91 percentage points since December 2023 [E39]. Technical momentum is also decidedly weak, with the stock trading below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E47] and suffering a 1-year compounded share price loss of -23% [E24]. conceded: [E42].

While the bear points to low historical return on equity figures [E25, E26, E27], those metrics ignore that a discounted cash flow analysis places intrinsic value at Rs 59 compared to a market price of Rs 32, offering a substantial 45.9% margin of safety [E42, E43]. The concern over recent profit contraction [E21, E65] overlooks the company's strong cash conversion of 2.33x for March 2026, which proves that its reported profits are fully backed by ₹ 21 Cr in operating cash flow and ₹ 6 Cr in free cash flow [E33, E34, E35]. Conceded: [E37]. Although borrowings increased and promoter holdings dipped [E37, E39], the stock trades at an attractive price-to-book ratio of 0.68x and an EV/EBITDA of 7.82x that both sit below sector benchmarks [E2, E7, E11]. Furthermore, the bear's emphasis on weak technical momentum [E47] misses the fundamental reality that 5-year profit growth of 14% has outpaced the 5-year share price decline of -14%, meaning fundamentals are outpacing the stock and signalling potential undervaluation [E22, E52].

The bull's reliance on a DCF intrinsic value of Rs 59 and a 45.9% margin of safety [E42, E43] ignores that the rules-based screen only scores the business at 64 out of 100 with low confidence [E60]. While operating cash flow reached Rs 21 Cr [E34], profit growth over the trailing twelve months contracted by -12% [E21], net profit dropped -30% year-over-year [E65], and sales fell -4% year-over-year [E66], demonstrating clear earnings deceleration [E67]. Conceded: [E7, E11, E52]. Although price-to-book and EV/EBITDA sit below sector benchmarks [E7, E11], and 5-year profit growth outpaced share price decline [E52], the fundamental reality is that the median return on equity has remained chronically low at 4% over the last 3, 5, and 10 years [E25, E26, E27], accompanied by a declining promoter stake down to 66.53% [E39] and rising borrowings of Rs 124 Cr [E37]. Furthermore, the company pays a 0.00% dividend yield [E4] despite reporting repeated profits [E57], and the stock trades below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E47].
